title: Possible safety hazard otherwise love it. See VIDEO
text:
Possible safety hazard otherwise love it. See VIDEO. [[VIDEOID:add165a37251916141d7ce73c55913b5]] I don't hate it. I will describe why I like it, then why I am giving it just 1 star.

Why I wanted it: We don't do much cooking in the microwave. We had a big microwave taking up precious counter real estate. We didn't want to out right get rid of it since we used it just enough to warrant keeping it. On occasion we use it to reheat something or when I don't feel like using the rice cooker, I will make it in the microwave instead. So my husband looked for a smaller microwave, and selected this one.

Dimensions are as described. As with any product, read the description and compare it to your needs and space. Rounded in the back, narrow width, tall height; more so than most microwaves. It fit snug under my kitchen cabinets. Pushed back into a corner, it freed up much desired space.

We use a lot of Corelle ware products. Fits their very large dinner plates,their regular sized dinner plates, 2 quart bowls, 1 quart bowls. Any other brand of plates have fit in there as well. No problem. Keep your item within the space of the rotating plate and you will be fine. There is no space outside of the rotating plate, so squares or rectangles may not advance.
Fits bags for steam vegetables, popcorn, and regular size mugs. Although a taller overall microwave (due to controls running along the bottom rather than the side), it is limited in height space. So no extra tall mugs.

None of that is a big deal if you are just looking for basic reheating or popcorn popping.

Controls are easy enough, I won't describe them here. Default tapping is 30 second increments. Option to change that, change wattage, etc.

Given all that, I would give it a solid 4 stars.

Why the reduction to 1 star? Possible safety hazard and major inconvenience at times.

Occasionally while the microwave has been cooking something the cooking time on the microwave will suddenly change. I didn't ask ti to add time. It just decided to do so. I have had an item in there set for say 3 minutes (could be less, could be more), then hear it reset itself to 30 minutes. Certainly not anything that requires cooking for 30 minutes in a microwave. I am just reheating! Not always 30, sometimes a bit less, but the take away here is that it is doing something that wasn't asked of it. It just suddenly adds a bunch of time. I had always been in the room when this happens except this last time, which reminded me and prompted me to write a review. I decided to make a large portion of oatmeal in the microwave rather than stove top because I needed to make use of that time to take a quick shower rather than stand at a stove. I thought I could let the oats cook for 5 minutes with extra water; basically get them started and I would finish them off when I was done with showering. . I came back into the kitchen about 15 minutes later and the oats were still cooking. The microwave had an additional 28 minutes left according to read out (originally only set for 5). I immediately took the oats out and they were shriveled up to the point of being garbage. Had I not come back right away to check on it how long would this have cooked for? Would it just keep adding time? How much would it take to burn out the microwave or do house damage? This has happened the times that I have tried to make rice. Set for 15 minutes, and then it adds time. Or the readout starts flicking and flashing and beeping. I think the moisture affects the sensors. Have never experienced such odd behavior from a microwave until now. It needs to cook for what I set it at. No more, no less.

How about this? When you set the timer on the microwave, it successfully cooks what is in there, then turns off when timer runs out. Pretty basic expectation, right? If you leave food in there after the timer runs down it gives out a beep- like most microwaves- to let you know something is still in there. However, with this microwave, it doesn't always just stop there. This one has also on occasion just decided to turn itself back on, and setting the timer to some random number between 20-30 minutes. So the thing you only needed to cook for one minute is now being cooked for 20-30 minutes (and more?!?!) if you don't go grab it out from microwave immediately.

How about when it is not in use at all? Well, getting steam or other moisture (say from a cleaning product) on the control panel will make it beep and make the controls change (say from 5w to 75, etc).

I don't know.. it is just concerning. I'm trying to remember to unplug it now when not in use, and watch and listen very closely when it is in use. For these reasons, the potential safety hazard, and the decrease in convenience, I can't give it more than one star. Hope this helps.

EDIT: I added a picture. Note that the time remaining says 24+ minutes. I set it for ONLY five minutes! I was heating halved acorn squash. So what the...?

EDIT #2: I added a video- we were finally able to catch the concerning behavior on video. Once again, we do not leave food unattended in microwave, even if the timer has reached zero and turned off. The microwave will turn back on and set itself for maximum time (30 minutes!). Who knows how long it would continue to do that?! This was a food item put in for 3 minutes. The microwave cooked the food, then shut off at end of timer. My husband and I had been prepping other foods, so didn't take it out immediately, but within a minute, it turned back on and set itself for 30 minutes to cook. We stopped the microwave and decided to see if we could catch it doing it again, so we set it for a minute, and sure enough the microwave decided to turn back on shortly after and set itself for maximum cook time. Can you imagine if it did that and the food ws allowed to cook in a microwave for that long above and beyond what you intended? This was some cut up vegertables, but can you imagine popcorn? So yeh, we still use the microwave but we are aware of this bizarro behavior.

product_metadata.title: Whirlpool WMC20005YW Countertop Microwave, 0.5 Cu. Ft., White
features: Tap Touch ControlsThese controls are as easy to use as they are to clean.10 - Level Variable Cooking Power ControlWith 10 variable power levels this microwave lets you quickly and easily tailor your cooking to the task at hand.Pocket Handle DoorControl LockDisables the control panel to avoid unintended use or other changes to your cooking settings.
description: Quickly set this Whirlpool(R) countertop microwave to cook for 30 seconds at 100% power with the Add 30 Seconds option. You can also press it to add 30 seconds to a manual setting that is already in progress. With 0.5 cu. ft. capacity, there's enough room for a dinner plate without taking up valuable counter space. Plus, the control lock feature helps you avoid unintended use or other changes to your cooking settings by disabling the control panel with the touch of a button.
